> Thanks again for the quick follow up. We have a small cross-region group (London, NYC, Singapore) that needs to attend a 45–60 minute demo...

Quick summary from our side: US moved to DST earlier this month (UTC-7 for Pacific / UTC-4 for Eastern), while many EU teams are still on standard time (UTC+1). That creates a one-week window where the nominal local time mapping shifts by one hour for attendees in the US vs EU. If you pick a CET time and assume US attendees have already shifted, you may accidentally schedule someone an hour earlier/later than expected.

Suggested options to avoid confusion:
- Option 1: Keep the current week but state the meeting time in UTC only (I can include the exact local conversions in the calendar invite).
- Option 2: Move to the week after EU switches (week of 30 Mar) so everyone uses the same DST status — fewer accidental no-shows.
- Option 3: Pick a window that minimizes pain for APAC (late UTC) and confirm SMEs can join early morning US if necessary.

Conservative recommendation: move to the week of 30 Mar or pick a UTC-first slot now so calendar clients don't auto-adjust incorrectly.

If helpful, here are a couple of concrete UTC-first slots we can offer (45 min demo + 15 min buffer):
- Tue 31 Mar 2026 15:00 UTC (Wed 01 Apr 00:00 SGT / Tue 31 Mar 16:00 CET / Tue 31 Mar 09:00 PDT)
- Wed 01 Apr 2026 13:00 UTC (Wed 01 Apr 22:00 SGT / Wed 01 Apr 14:00 CET / Wed 01 Apr 07:00 PDT)

Please let me know which you'd prefer and I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in + an explicit UTC header.

Thanks,
